fact: Legal name: William Marsh Rice University. Private, nonprofit, nonsectarian research university.
Founded 1912 (chartered 1891; opened September 23, 1912). Named for William Marsh Rice, a Houston merchant murdered in 1900 whose bequest funded the university.
Located at 6100 Main Street, Houston, Texas 77005; 300-acre campus adjacent to the Texas Medical Center and Houston Museum District
Total enrollment Fall 2025: approximately 8,880 students — ~4,807 undergraduates and ~4,264 graduate/professional students
Endowment: $8.07 billion (FY2024); FY2025 investment return 11.4%; endowment covers more than 40% of annual operating budget
Annual operating budget: approximately $1.09 billion (FY2025)
US News National University Ranking: #17 (2026 edition); #16 (2027 edition)
Acceptance rate: 8.0% (2025-26 cycle; 36,791 applications received, 2,948 admitted)
Undergraduate tuition and fees: $70,720 (2026-27 academic year)
The Rice Investment: families with income below $75,000 pay no tuition, fees, room, or board; families $75,000-$140,000 pay no tuition; families $140,000-$200,000 get at least half tuition covered
Rice meets 100% of demonstrated financial need and does not include loans in any need-based financial aid package (loan-free since Fall 2022)
45% of first-year students receive need-based aid; average net price for federal loan recipients ~$15,091
Total grant aid to undergraduates projected at approximately $174 million in FY2026
Student-to-faculty ratio: 6:1; full-time faculty: 912
11 residential colleges (12th, Chao College, under construction for 2026); all entering students randomly assigned and remain members for life

8 academic schools: Humanities, Social Sciences, Natural Sciences, George R. Brown School of Engineering and Computing, Shepherd School of Music, Architecture, Jones Graduate School of Business, Glasscock School of Continuing Studies
29 PhD programs offered
Research expenditures: $277.7 million total R&D (FY2024), up from $255.1 million in FY2023
SAT middle 50% (enrolled, 2025-26 CDS): 1510-1560 composite; 740-770 EBRW, 760-800 Math
ACT middle 50% (enrolled): 34-36 composite
4-year graduation rate: approximately 85-87%
NCAA Division I-FBS; member of the American Athletic Conference; nickname: Owls
2 Nobel Prizes in Chemistry connected to Rice: Robert F. Curl Jr. and Richard E. Smalley (Rice faculty; 1996 Nobel Chemistry for discovery of buckminsterfullerene/buckyballs)
Notable alumni: Larry McMurtry (Pulitzer Prize), James A. Baker III (US Secretary of State), Peggy Whitson (NASA astronaut), John Doerr (venture capitalist)
Rice returned to test-required for Fall 2026 entry (with hardship exceptions)
Baker Institute for Public Policy: one of the nation's top-ranked university-based public policy think tanks, named for alumnus James Baker
